run: the XTTS check: does ParsVoice-XTTS, the most Persian-trained cloning model found, read news better than the app
status: registered 2026-10-25, before any front-end ran on these sentences and before any render
why: the news vowels check (FINDINGS section 21) left about one word in ten wrong on news text in every form, and showed that more marks make OmniVoice worse; what is left is the model's own reading. Bases checked live the same day (SOTA_ROADMAP section 4): Fish Audio Drama 3 lists Persian but fits neither this Mac nor Kaggle's T4s; ParsVoice-XTTS (XTTS-v2 adapted on about 2,000 h of Persian audiobooks, 1,800+ speakers; arXiv 2510.10774) is the most Persian-trained cloning model found and fits; Audio8-TTS-Persian is left out because it was trained on Mana-TTS, the voice every listening test here clones, and its card calls its cloning of unseen voices weak

sentences.written_by: Claude, 2026-10-25: news in ten fields (inflation, a software release, football, flu, a fast train, traffic, a book fair, a Mars launch, gold, schools), with Western months, borrowed names and two numbers; none of the user's own sentences
sentences.leakage_rule: letters only, equal or one inside the other with at least 20 letters and half the longer - step 2's rule

forms.O: the app today: OmniVoice with the adaptation's step-1,000 weights (A1) reading the app's text - the tagger's ezafe, the homograph first vowels, the number fixes
forms.X: ParsVoice-XTTS (MohammadJRanjbar/ParsVoice-XTTS, gated, accepted by the user) reading the app's normalised text with no marks - numbers already words, since its tokenizer only lowercases Persian - with Persian punctuation mapped and its inference settings as in its own notebook (temperature 0.1, top_k 10, top_p 0.3, repetition_penalty 10, length_penalty 1), through the XTTS fork it was trained with

voice: mana_000.wav for both, each prepared as its own code prepares a reference (the app's reference pipeline for O; 24 kHz mono at -20 dBFS RMS for X, as its notebook does)
rendering: O on Kaggle T4 x2 as the adapted reading check (render_frontend_conditions.py with the A1 export, seed 42); X on this Mac on CPU, because the gated weights are fetched here with the user's token and are not re-hosted: the training checkpoint (5.7 GB with its optimizer) is read memory-mapped and its model weights saved alone, and the render stops if available memory falls under 3.4 GB or pressure reaches warning; seed 42. CER for both on this Mac with faster-whisper large-v3-turbo (int8) after both are collected, so one recogniser scores both; held-out similarity on this Mac as before
review: as before: the plain sentence, two readings in Latin-square slots (each form five times in each slot), loudness matched, the key off the page; words to tap, a note, the better reading

decision_rule.primary: words marked wrong per form, of 169 per listener who answers all 10 sentences
decision_rule.rule: X replaces OmniVoice as the app's Persian engine if it has fewer words marked wrong than O and is not flagged. A tie keeps O
decision_rule.harm: X is flagged, and not adopted without the user's say, if its mean CER is more than 2 points above O's, or if its paired held-out similarity difference against O has a 95% bootstrap interval wholly below zero (10,000 resamples, seed 20261003). If X has fewer words wrong but is flagged, both numbers go to the user, who decides

read_beside_it_not_for_the_decision: the words each form got wrong, the picked readings, the notes
not_claimed: one voice (mana), one seed, 169 words of news, the listeners who answer; XTTS-v2's licence (CPML) is non-commercial
cost: Kaggle: one session, about 0.2 GPU-hours; this Mac: about 6 GB of disk for the XTTS environment and weights; listening about 10 minutes
